title: The Founding Documents of the United States of America
author: Study the Great Books
summary: This essay argues that America's founding documents — the Declaration of Independence, the Constitution, and the Federalist/Anti-Federalist debate — represent an unprecedented achievement in political history, made possible by the Founders' deep classical education. The author contends that today's civic ignorance about these documents correlates directly with rising socialist and Marxist sentiment, since a historically illiterate populace lacks the intellectual defenses against bad ideas repackaged by unscrupulous politicians. The piece traces the Founders' intellectual formation through the Bible, Plato and Aristotle, Roman history and Cicero, medieval thinkers like Augustine, Boethius, and Aquinas, and Enlightenment figures such as Locke, Montesquieu, Hume, and Hobbes. It presents this classical liberal education — not the documents alone — as the true wellspring of America's success. The essay is explicitly framed as an argument for the ongoing relevance of Great Books study to civic and political health.
points: Argues that ignorance of America's founding documents is directly linked to the rise of socialism and Marxism in contemporary politics.
Frames Great Books education as a civic 'mental bulwark' that inoculates citizens against demagogues repackaging failed ideas.

Traces the Founders' intellectual formation through Scripture, Greek philosophy (Plato, Aristotle), Roman history and Cicero, medieval thought (Augustine, Boethius, Aquinas), and Enlightenment philosophy (Locke, Montesquieu, Hume, Hobbes).
Credits America's founding success not to the documents themselves but to the classical liberal education that produced the men who wrote them.
Positions the Declaration, Constitution, and Federalist/Anti-Federalist Papers as the practical fruit of centuries of Western political philosophy.
quotes: There is a direct correlation between the growing ignorance concerning the content of our nation's foundational documents amidst our citizenry and the dramatic increase in socialism and even outright Marxism in America's political landscape.
A people ignorant of their own history, not to mention history in general, are a people that are vulnerable to old and bad ideas that have been tried and found wanting.

It's easy for wicked and unprincipled men to dress up bad ideas and make them palatable to the masses when the populous has not developed the needful mental bulwarks against lupine politicians that come as a result of studying the Great Books.

The United States of America has been an unprecedented success because our founding fathers were not ignorant of history. Our founders were liberally educated men who had studied the western canon of literature.

They had studied the Bible along with its political principles and concepts, they read Plato and Aristotle and the other great political philosophers of the ancient Greeks, they studied the rise and fall of Rome as it went from a monarchy to a republic to an empire.

Our founders were steeped in the great conversation of political philosophy and theory throughout the ages, they paid attention to past successes and failures in regard to what makes a people free and prosperous, and they put together the single greatest country the world has ever seen when it comes to creating liberty and justice for all.
